problem: Prior audio-visual simulators were too rigid for embodied learning. SoundSpaces 1.0 pre-computed RIRs on a 0.5 m grid for a fixed set of 100 Replica/Matterport3D scenes, which forced grid-hopping agents, gave no transfer to new meshes, took TBs of storage and allowed no change of materials or microphones. ThreeDWorld renders audio continuously but only for 'shoebox' rooms, so it cannot be used with real-scan datasets (Gibson, HM3D).
motivation: Joint visual-acoustic simulation lets audio-visual embodied tasks (AV navigation, mapping, localization, separation, acoustic matching) be trained at scale and reproducibly, and it is a route to sim2real. Grid-based, pre-rendered audio removes hard parts of the task: agents never collide, localization is implicitly perfect, and the audio is not acoustically continuous. Real-world fidelity of simulated RIRs had also never been checked against real measurements.
key_idea: Replace pre-computed grid RIRs with an on-the-fly bidirectional path-tracing audio engine (RLR-Audio-Propagation) inside Habitat-Sim that works for any mesh, at any continuous source/receiver pose, with configurable materials and microphones, and with acoustically continuous audio streams.
insight: Continuity matters for audio-visual navigation. A DAV-Nav agent trained on discrete SoundSpaces still reaches 64.2% SR in continuous space, but its SPL drops to 27.5 (vs 49.3 when trained in SoundSpaces 2.0). It collapses to 0.9% SR when the audio is acoustically continuous, because it relied on an always-present direct-sound cue that is now mixed with reverberation. Physical-fidelity fixes also pay off: adding diffraction and removing a sqrt(4π) bias in indirect pressure cuts DRR error against real Replica measurements from 11.0 dB to 0.98 dB, with RT60 error unchanged at 12.4%. The fidelity transfers to real data: ASR fine-tuned on SS2.0 IRs beats fine-tuning on real IRs (12.48 vs 13.32 WER). Structured acoustic randomization (plausible per-category materials plus N(0,0.1) coefficient noise) helps further (12.04), whereas uniform coefficient randomization hurts (12.58).
method: RLR-Audio-Propagation engine: energy-based bidirectional path tracing. Source rays and listener rays carry log-spaced frequency-band energy and undergo Phong-BRDF reflection, probabilistic edge diffraction and transmission. Paths are connected with multiple importance sampling into an energy-time histogram with spherical-harmonic directivity; early reflections (≤2 bounces) and direct sound are handled separately.

IR synthesis & spatialization: the energy histogram is converted to a pressure IR (square root plus band-filtered noise for phase). The result is spatialized to ambisonic or binaural using an HRTF; the direct sound keeps barycentric HRTF interpolation. Custom HRTFs and 7 microphone layouts (mono…ambisonics) or user mic arrays are supported.

Simulation fixes over SoundSpaces 1.0: fast diffraction (Schissler 2021) so occluded sources no longer cut off abruptly, and removal of a sqrt(4π) bias in indirect sound pressure to correct the direct-to-reverberant ratio.

Spatial + acoustic continuity: RIRs R(s,r,θ) are rendered at arbitrary poses. Per step, N=FΔt source samples (the continuing source-signal segment) are convolved without zero padding, and consecutive-pose outputs are linearly crossfaded, so the source emits continuously while the agent moves.

Configurability: sampling rate, frequency bands, ray counts/depths and effect toggles are exposed. There are 29 built-in acoustic materials with frequency-dependent absorption/scattering/transmission/damping coefficients, a category-to-material mapping API, analytical air absorption, and shoebox-room APIs.

Rendering modes: 'high-quality' uses maximum rays and no temporal coherence. 'High-speed' reuses previous-frame paths/IRs (temporal coherence) with fewer rays, giving 7.7 FPS (1 thread) / 33.5 FPS (5 threads) vs 0.9 / 4.0 at 9.5% relative RT60 error.

Assets/benchmarks: a continuous AV-Nav task (0.15 m forward / 10° turns, 1 m success radius) trained with a DD-PPO DAV-Nav agent; the SoundSpaces-PanoIR dataset (10M panoramic RGB-D + IR pairs from 750 MP3D/Gibson/HM3D scenes); real IR measurements in the Replica FRL apartment; a far-field ASR sim2real benchmark with acoustic randomization.

numbers_note: This is a simulator paper. The nav split is not stated (reported as 'test'), and the nav number is for a new continuous AV-Nav task, not the original discrete SoundSpaces AudioGoal benchmark. Simulation-fidelity numbers are not benchmark entries: Table 2 speed/quality tradeoff; DRR error 11.0→0.98 dB and RT60 error 12.4% vs real Replica IRs, given only in text and figures (Fig. 3b, supp. figure). The DAV-Nav rows trained on discrete SoundSpaces (64.2/27.5/5.6 continuous space; 0.9/0.3/12.9 with continuous sound) are baseline conditions and are omitted.
results: On continuous AV-Nav, the DAV-Nav agent trained in SoundSpaces 2.0 reaches 64.7% SR / 49.3 SPL / 5.9 m DTG. The same agent trained on discrete SoundSpaces gets 64.2 SR / 27.5 SPL with continuous motion only, and collapses to 0.9% SR / 0.3 SPL when the sound is also acoustically continuous. For far-field ASR sim2real, fine-tuning on SS2.0 IRs gives 12.48% WER, beating real IRs (13.32), Pyroomacoustics (16.24), SoundSpaces 1.0 (18.48) and the pretrained model (29.10); acoustic randomization lowers it to 12.04%. Against real Replica measurements, DRR error falls from 11.0 dB to 0.98 dB, and high-speed mode is 8×/33× faster than high-quality mode at 9.5% relative RT60 error.
limitations: Accuracy depends on mesh quality: holes leak rays, e.g. Matterport3D yields systematically lower RT60s. Material properties cannot be inferred from meshes, so category-level default or randomized materials are assumed. Geometric acoustics still misses wave effects such as room modes.
Real-world validation covers a single apartment (Replica FRL) at 7 source/receiver positions, with materials optimized to match; the RT60 error (12.4%) is not improved over SoundSpaces 1.0.

The navigation benchmark is thin: one agent (DAV-Nav), one training seed, split/scene dataset not specified. High-speed mode (~33 FPS with 5 threads) is far slower than pre-rendered SoundSpaces (500+ FPS), and there is no real-robot validation of navigation.
compares_to: ASR fine-tuned on real IRs (Ko et al. 2017)
